sentences.text: In 2024, the influence index stands at 24.4 for China (band 17.4–42.8, from 4 of six components) and 50.0 for the United States (band 44.8–80.1, from 4 of six components). The net lean is -25.6 points toward the United States.
Over the five years to 2024, the index for China was broadly flat and the index for the United States rose by 32.7 points.

The value for China rests on trade export share, trade import share, debt stock and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.

The value for the United States rests on trade export share, trade import share, finance flow and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.
In 2025, 0.0% of El Salvador's mineral exports (UN Comtrade value US$0 m) went to China and 5.3% to the United States; together 5.3%, the rest to other destinations.
Since 2020 the share going to China was broadly flat and the share going to the United States fell by 93.4 points.
Relative to the 20-country export basket, its exports are specialised in rare earths (RCA 6136.4) and gallium germanium antimony (RCA 108.0).
The AidData records show US$283 m of documented commitments from Chinese institutions to El Salvador over 2015–2021 (28 events; the source ends in 2021).
The DFC and EXIM records show US$1.8 bn of documented commitments from US institutions to El Salvador over 2007–2026 (166 events).
Public and publicly guaranteed external debt owed to China was 0.0% of GDP in 2024 (World Bank IDS); no comparable series exists for debt owed to the United States.

The lenders with the largest recorded commitments to named recipients here are US International Development Finance Corporation (US$1.2 bn), China Ministry of Commerce (US$627 m) and OPIC (predecessor of DFC) (US$566 m).
Flags: documented commitments reached at least 1% of GDP in a year in 2019 and 2024 (documented).
In the UN General Assembly, voting agreement in 2024 was 79% with China and 38% with the United States.
Since 2019, agreement with China fell by 5.6 points and agreement with the United States rose by 14.2 points.
Too few mineral-related legislative records naming either actor have been scored for a stance series (five per year are needed); the text model is zero-shot baseline, not yet validated.

After China: exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the United States prohibited (Announcement 2024 No. 46) (2024-12), the share of exports to the United States moved -91.3 points (97% before, 5.3% after); placebo p 0.14 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: export controls on antimony items in force (Announcement 2024 No. 33 of 15 August 2024) (2024-09), the share of exports to the United States moved -91.3 points (97% before, 5.3% after); placebo p 0.14 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: export controls on graphite items in force (Announcement 2023 No. 39 of 20 October 2023) (2023-12), the share of exports to the United States moved -49.0 points (99% before, 50% after); placebo p 0.48 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to the United States in 2030 is 12% (90% band 0.0%–100%), from naive persistence, because no model beat it in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.

The published forecast for the influence index of China in 2030 is 26.9 (90% band 11.4–41.0), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 1% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

The published forecast for the influence index of the United States in 2030 is 39.8 (90% band 13.3–65.4), from damped local linear trend (Kalman filter, maximum likelihood), which beat naive persistence by 2% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

In 2025, unavailable components: legislative stance (no scored legislative records naming the actor); debt stock (no source for debt owed to the United States); finance flow (source coverage ends 2021); debt stock and diplomatic alignment (source coverage ends 2024).

Source coverage ends at different years: Chinese official finance to 2021, US finance to 2026, debt by creditor to 2024, UN votes to 2024 and trade to 2025; components beyond a source's coverage are unavailable, not zero.
12 of the dated events used above are still in the draft event list awaiting the project owner's review.
Stance values come from the text model (zero-shot baseline, not yet validated); the rest of this brief rests on official statistics and the registered databases, each cited on its chart.
